definition: Arabic written in Latin letters with digits standing in for Arabic-specific sounds (3 = ع, 7 = ح, 2 = ء): "3amel eh".
details: Arabic written in Latin letters with digits standing in for Arabic-specific sounds (3 = ع, 7 = ح, 2 = ء): "3amel eh". Common in chat and social data; systems either normalize it via transliteration or must be trained to understand it natively.

explainer.lead: Arabizi is a way to write Arabic with Latin letters, using digits for sounds that Latin spelling does not easily cover. It matters for language technology because chat and social-media text may not look like standard Arabic script, so systems must either convert it or learn to handle it directly.

tiers.eli5: Imagine writing a language with a keyboard that does not have all its letters. You could use numbers as stand-ins, a bit like using 3 for one special sound and 7 for another. Arabizi is that kind of workaround for Arabic, and computers need special handling to read it.
tiers.practitioner: Arabizi appears in chat and social data, so an Arabic NLP pipeline should not assume that all input is in Arabic script. One option is to normalize it through transliteration; another is to train the system to understand Arabizi natively. A pitfall is treating its digits as ordinary numbers rather than possible markers for Arabic-specific sounds.
tiers.paperLevel: Arabizi is a Latin-script representation of Arabic augmented by digit-to-sound mappings, including 3 = ع, 7 = ح, and 2 = ء. For NLP, the input can be mapped through transliteration into normalized text or retained as Arabizi for native modeling. These alternatives differ in whether conversion is performed before downstream processing.

explainer.example: In “3amel eh”, the digit 3 stands for the Arabic letter ع; the rest is written with Latin letters. The digit is therefore part of the word’s spelling, not a quantity to be read as “three”.

usedIn.name: Chat data
usedIn.detail: Arabizi is common in informal messages written with Latin letters and digits.

usedIn.name: Social-media analysis
usedIn.detail: Systems processing social data may encounter Arabizi alongside other text.

usedIn.name: Arabic NLP pipelines
usedIn.detail: Inputs can be normalized by transliteration or handled directly by models trained on Arabizi.

explainer.intuition: Arabizi improvises an Arabic spelling system on a Latin keyboard: familiar letters carry much of the writing, while selected digits represent Arabic sounds that need extra symbols.
howItWorks: Write Arabic words using Latin letters.
Use digits for certain Arabic-specific sounds.
Read mappings such as 3 = ع, 7 = ح, and 2 = ء according to context.
For NLP, either transliterate the text to normalize it or process it directly with a system trained on Arabizi.
explainer.whyItMatters: Arabizi is common in chat and social data, which makes it a practical input format for Arabic language systems. Choosing between transliteration-based normalization and native handling determines whether this text can be processed effectively.
misconceptions: The digits are not necessarily numbers; in Arabizi they can stand for Arabic sounds.
Arabizi is not Arabic written in the standard Arabic alphabet.
Converting Arabizi is not the only option: a system can instead be trained to understand it natively.

diagram.caption: An NLP system can normalize Arabizi through transliteration or learn to handle the original text directly.
